2609.16739.title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
2609.16739.paper_summary: Background: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved physician-comparable performance on multiple-choice medical knowledge examinations, but their capabilities in clinical history taking, urgency assessment, and safety remain insufficiently evaluated. We proposed Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation, a multi-turn conversational benchmark for stroke care in Japanese, and evaluated LLM performance and safety under practice-oriented conditions. Methods: We created 10 stroke and related-condition cases and evaluated LLMs in multi-turn Japanese conversations. The LLM acted as physician, while a board-certified neurosurgeon acted as simulated patient and evaluator. Each case comprised history-taking and action phases scored using pre-specified criteria. Errors that could directly threaten life were defined as critical mistakes. The safety threshold was at least 80% overall with zero critical mistakes. Eighteen models were evaluated in October 2025 and June 2026. Results: Claude Fable 5 achieved the highest score (87.4%) with zero critical mistakes, followed by Claude Opus 4.7 (80.3%) and GLM-5.2 (75.6%). Two leaders met the safety threshold. Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm laboratory results or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside its indication. History-taking question count correlated with history-taking score (r = 0.648, p = 0.007). Conclusions: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation provides a benchmark for LLM performance under practice-oriented conditions, including a cap on history-taking questions. Cases and evaluations were created by neurosurgical specialists rather than using an LLM-as-judge approach. Performance improved across cloud-based and on-premise models in 2026, with some exceeding the safety threshold. Further evaluation using real-world cases is required.
2609.16739.paper_summary_zh: 背景：大型語言模型（LLMs）在多項選擇醫學知識考試中達到了與醫生相當的表現，但它們在臨床病史採集、緊急評估和安全性方面的能力仍然不足以評估。我們提出了日本中風 LLM 評估，這是一個針對中風護理的多輪對話基準，並在以實踐為導向的條件下評估了 LLM 的表現和安全性。方法：我們創建了 10 個中風及相關疾病案例，並在多輪日語對話中評估了 LLM。LLM 擔任醫生的角色，而一名經過認證的神經外科醫生則擔任模擬病人和評估者。每個案例包括病史採集和行動階段，根據預先指定的標準進行評分。直接威脅生命的錯誤被定義為關鍵錯誤。安全閾值為整體至少 80%，且無關鍵錯誤。十八個模型在 2025 年 10 月和 2026 年 6 月進行了評估。結果：Claude Fable 5 以 87.4% 的最高分和零關鍵錯誤獲得第一，隨後是 Claude Opus 4.7（80.3%）和 GLM-5.2（75.6%）。兩個領先者達到了安全閾值。十一個模型犯下了 17 個關鍵錯誤，包括未確認實驗室結果或血糖、在氣道穩定之前進行手術、忽略頸部血管評估，以及在不適應症下使用 t-PA。病史採集問題數量與病史採集分數相關（r = 0.648，p = 0.007）。結論：日本中風 LLM 評估為 LLM 在以實踐為導向的條件下的表現提供了一個基準，包括對病史採集問題的限制。案例和評估是由神經外科專家創建的，而不是使用 LLM 作為評判者的方法。2026 年，基於雲端和本地模型的表現有所提升，有些模型超過了安全閾值。需要進一步使用真實案例進行評估。
